title: Big Shifts in Big Tech Today

slides.headline: Big Shifts in Big Tech Today
slides.subtitle: From gaming slumps to new AI tools, here is what moved the needle this week.

slides.headline: Meta faces pushback on AI costs
slides.explanation: Meta shares dipped as investors worry about the massive spending required for AI development. Mark Zuckerberg also revealed plans to start selling AI tools directly to other businesses.

slides.headline: Microsoft plans a Copilot super app
slides.explanation: A new all-in-one app is coming this year to combine chat, coding, and agent tools. It aims to streamline how you use AI for both work and personal projects.

slides.headline: Xbox revenue takes a hit
slides.explanation: Gaming revenue and hardware sales both dropped for Microsoft this quarter. This shows the company is leaning much harder into cloud services and AI than traditional console gaming.

slides.headline: Microsoft profits from AI bets
slides.explanation: Microsoft gained over 3 billion dollars from its investment in Anthropic this year. It shows how the company is diversifying its AI portfolio beyond just its partnership with OpenAI.

slides.headline: Meta eyes the enterprise market
slides.explanation: Beyond just building agents, Meta is looking to sell software and computing power to businesses. It is a clear sign they want to be a major infrastructure provider for companies.

caption:
Big tech is moving fast this week, with major pivots in gaming and artificial intelligence. We are seeing a clear shift toward enterprise tools and away from traditional hardware. Which of these updates surprised you the most?

title: Interest Rates, Fraud, and Global Tensions

slides.headline: Interest Rates, Fraud, and Global Tensions
slides.subtitle: Get the latest on the economy and world events in under two minutes.

slides.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady
slides.explanation: The Fed voted to keep interest rates unchanged for the fifth time since December. This decision reflects ongoing concerns about inflation and the impact of rising energy prices.

slides.headline: Inflation Remains a Key Concern
slides.explanation: The Fed says that supply shocks are keeping inflation levels high. This matters because it directly impacts the cost of energy and everyday goods for consumers.

slides.headline: Film Financier Indicted in Fraud Case
slides.explanation: Producer Jason Cloth has been indicted for his alleged role in a 100 million dollar Ponzi scheme. He is known for financing major films like Joker and Ghostbusters: Afterlife.

slides.headline: Sentencing in NY Headquarters Ramming
slides.explanation: A New Jersey man received a six-month sentence for driving his car into a Chabad Lubavitch building. The incident caused significant damage to the entrance of the world headquarters.

slides.headline: Trump Issues New Warning to Iran
slides.explanation: Donald Trump has threatened to hit Iran very hard amid rising geopolitical tensions. This highlights the fragile state of international relations and potential energy market instability.

caption:
From the latest economic policy shifts to breaking legal news, here are the stories shaping the headlines today. We break down the facts so you can stay informed without the noise. Which of these updates did you find most surprising?
